questions.html:
Consider the following statements:
1. The redundancy in the set of relation that have been arised after decomposing a relation R into BCNF is zero irrespective of the type of dependencies.
2. BCNF decompositions are always lossless as well as dependency preserving.
3. A prime attribute of a relation schema R is an attribute that appears in all candidate key of R.
4. A relation R is in 3NF, if every non-prime attribute of R, is fully functionally dependent on some key of R.
The number of statements are correct _______.
questions.solution:
1
1. The redundancy in the set of relation that have been arised after decomposing a relation R into BCNF is more than zero but less than 3NF decomposition if multivalued dependencies are considered.
2. BCNF decompositions are lossless but always need not to be dependency preserving.
3. A prime attribute of a relation schema R is an attribute that appears in some candidate key of R.
4. A relation R is in 3NF, if every non-prime attribute of R, is fully functionally dependent on some key, because then there will be no transitive dependency.

questions.solution:

questions.html: Which of the following is an accurate description of the equal-width binning method in discretization?

options.html: The range of data is divided into intervals of equal size, and each data point is assigned to the corresponding interval.
Data is grouped based on frequency, ensuring each bin contains an equal number of data points.
Data points are assigned to bins based on their proximity to the bin's mean value.
The data range is split into bins based on predefined thresholds that vary in width.

questions.solution:
(a)
(a) Equal-width binning divides the entire data range into intervals (bins) of equal size, with each data point assigned to the appropriate bin based on its value. So, option (a) is correct.
(b) This describes equal-frequency binning, not equal-width binning. So, option (b) is incorrect.
(c) Bins in equal-width binning are not based on proximity to a mean but are of uniform width.
So, option (c) is incorrect.
(d) In equal-width binning, the intervals have the same width, not varying widths. So, option (d) is incorrect.

questions.tags: Technical • Data Science and artificial Intelligence • +1 / -0.33
questions.html: In binning, which of the following methods replaces each value in a bin with the bin’s mean value?
questions.solution:
(a)
(a) Mean binning replaces each value in a bin with the mean (average) value of all the data points within that bin. So, option (a) is correct.
(b) Median binning would replace each value with the median, not the mean. So, option (b) is incorrect.
(c) Equal-width binning refers to dividing the data range into equal-sized bins, not replacing values with the mean. So, option (c) is incorrect.
(d) Frequency binning refers to bins containing equal numbers of data points, not mean replacement. So, option (d) is incorrect.

questions.tags: Technical • Data Science and artificial Intelligence • +2 / -0
questions.html: Which of the following are true about the data storage in OLTP systems?

options.html: OLTP systems use normalized tables to reduce redundancy.
OLTP systems store historical data for long-term analysis.
OLTP systems require efficient indexing to ensure fast data retrieval.
OLTP systems are typically used for strategic decision-making.

questions.solution:
(a, c)
(a) OLTP systems use normalized tables to reduce data redundancy and ensure data integrity. So, option (a) is correct.
(b) OLTP systems focus on current transaction data, not on storing historical data for long-term analysis, which is more typical of OLAP systems. So, option (b) is incorrect.
(c) Efficient indexing is crucial in OLTP systems to allow for quick retrieval of transaction data.
So, option (c) is correct.
(d) OLTP systems are used for day-to-day transaction processing, not for strategic decisionmaking, which is the role of OLAP systems. So, option (d) is incorrect.
